Chopin — Waltz No. 3, Op. 34

Tatyana's Letter

Translated from the Russian

I write to you — what more is there to say?
How shall I add to my confession?
I know it's in your power today
To punish me with your derision.

Yet if compassion plays a part
In your thoughts, you would not wait
To abandon me to fate.

At first I wished to stay quite silent;
Believe me, you would never have heard
Of shame or misery, one word.

If I'd reserved a hope, content
To see you but once a week,
To be in your presence, hear you speak,
Utter a few words of greeting,
And then, while you were gone,
Have that to think upon,
Day and night, till our next meeting.

You're unsociable, they say,
That the country bores you sadly;
And we… don't shine in any way,
Although we welcome you so gladly.

Why did you come to disturb us?
In this forgotten rural place
I'd not have known you, thus
Would not have known this bitter case.

In time the heart's confusion
Might have calmed: I would have found
Another, and been a true companion,
A faithful wife, a mother sound.

Another! … No, no there's none
On earth but you my heart adores!
That was ordained by fate alone…
It's Heaven's will: I am yours.

My life was but a pledge till now
Of our prophetic meeting: yes,
God sent you to me, I avow,
Till in the grave we shall rest…

You appeared to me in dreaming,
Already dear, though still unseen,
Your wondrous gaze set me trembling,
Your voice disturbed my soul's serene
Long, long ago… No, that was not
A dream! Scarce had you entered, I knew,
I was all confusion, I burned, I thought:
It's him! And my heart spoke true.

Was it not you, in the silence, speaking
When I helped the poor, or when
I sought in prayer, my spirit seeking
To calm the anguish of my pain?
And at that very moment, was it not
Your image, clear, that seemed to shine,
Stole softly to my bedside, sat,
And whispered hope and love divine?

Who are you? My guardian angel, true,
Or some insidious tempter? Resolve
My doubts… It may be you
Are all an empty dream of love,
The fate of an inexperienced heart…
But so be it! From this hour
I entrust to you my destiny's part,
I beg your protection, I pour
My tears before you, I implore…

Imagine: I am here alone,
No one understands me, none,
My mind is failing, I must own,
And I must perish in silence, one
Who waits for you. Speak one word
To revive my hopes, or break
This heavy dream — alas, deserved
Reproach! I finish… I fear to take
Another look… I freeze with shame
And dread… But your honour is my trust,
And boldly to it I resign my name…
